details: For L>=1 the endpoint convention gives $\mathrm T\ge\lfloor\log_2\mathrm L\rfloor-1$ and the safe consequence $\mathrm T\ge(1/3)\log_2\mathrm L$. The former coefficient 1/2 is not justified by the cited capped-threshold proof; this correction does not claim it false or the new constant optimal.
proof: The cited capped-threshold theorem gives T_cap>=floor(log_2 L), and deleting its constant cap column gives T>=T_cap-1. Also L>=1 implies two different concepts, hence T>=1. For 1<=L<4 this implies T>=(log_2 L)/3. For q=floor(log_2 L)>=2, T>=q-1>=(q+1)/3>(log_2 L)/3. This is a safe derived bound, not an optimal-constant claim. At L=0 the logarithmic relation is inapplicable.
name: Threshold Dimension / Littlestone Dimension
proof_source: LaTeX survey, Lemma lem:endpoint-threshold-littlestone. Stored Alon et al. source, Theorem 3.2 in the archived version (Theorem 8 in the publication source map), uses capped thresholds. The endpoint translation loses at most one.
